content: What is your current job and daily workflow?

Okay, so my main thing right now is being a Computer Science student at the university. That's my full-time gig, basically. But to cover my rent and groceries and stuff, I also work part-time as a barista at a cafe not too far from campus.

My daily workflow is... pretty packed, honestly. A typical day usually starts with classes, which can be anywhere from 9 AM to late afternoon. My CS courses are pretty demanding, so there's always lectures, labs, and group projects. I try to get to the library or a study spot on campus between classes if I have a gap, just to squeeze in some homework or readings.

Then, depending on the day, I'll either head straight to my barista shift after classes, or I'll try to get a quick dinner or study session in first. My shifts are usually 4-5 hours long, a few times a week. At the cafe, it's pretty standard barista stuff: making coffees, taking orders, cleaning, stocking, dealing with the rushes when everyone's grabbing their caffeine fix. It can get pretty hectic, especially around lunchtime or late afternoon.

After work, it's usually back to my shared apartment. I'll either cook something quick – or grab something cheap if I'm too tired – and then it's usually more studying, coding, or working on assignments until pretty late. Sometimes I have to pull an all-nighter if there's a big project due. It's a constant juggle trying to balance my coursework with needing to earn money. Efficiency is key, otherwise I'd never get anything done!
